repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
API keys can be created without names using grant API key action. This is considered as a bug (#59484). Since the feature has already been released, we need to accomodate existing keys that are created with null names. This PR relaxes the parser logic so that a `null` name is accepted.

Resolves: #59481

issue.title: Regression when an API key has no name

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/58156 introduced a regression causing the following errors within Kibana:

```
   │ info [o.e.x.s.a.AuthenticationService] [desktop] Authentication using apikey failed - apikey authentication for id NB-BSnMBuA9FcpEJrQtR encountered a failure
   │      org.elasticsearch.common.xcontent.XContentParseException: [1:532] [api_key_doc] name doesn't support values of type: VALUE_NULL
```

These failures are being tracked in https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/71559, https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/71558 and https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/71555

issue.title: Return API key name in _authentication response

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Responses to POST /_security/api_key includes id, name, metadata,
api_key (shared secret), and encoded (base64 of id:api_key).

Requests to GET /_security/_authenticate returns data about the user,
but not the API KEY.

When authenticating using an API KEY, return API KEY info map in the
response. The initial feature request asked for 'name'. However, the
request's Authentication header contains 'encoded', so the decoded
'id' will be returned for convenience too.

When authenticating using any other method, API KEY info map is
omitted.

Closes #70306

Example request:
```
curl -s -X GET -H "Authorization: ApiKey base64(id:api_key)" "localhost:9200/_security/_authenticate?pretty"
```

Example response:
```
{
  "username" : "my-username",
  "roles" : [ ],
  "full_name" : null,
  "email" : null,
  "metadata" : { },
  "enabled" : true,
  "authentication_realm" : {
    "name" : "_es_api_key",
    "type" : "_es_api_key"
  },
  "lookup_realm" : {
    "name" : "_es_api_key",
    "type" : "_es_api_key"
  },
  "authentication_type" : "api_key",
  "token" : {
  },
  "api_key" : {
    "id": "jdgWKXwBtdtKDGAHT5OX"
    "name": "my-api-key"
  }
}
```
